（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY 7802 D. 110 Date July 1st 1940）

Subject Shun Pao - Notice re naturalisation in China of a German-
Jew appearing on 28.6.40

Made by D.S. Pharazyn Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Reference the query of P.A. to D.C. (Special
Branch) appended to attached translation of a notice
appearing in the Shun Pao of 28.6.40 in connection with
the naturalisation of one "Hanna" in China, enquiries
made by C.D.C. 230 Chang Yeh show that the advertiser
is named Hannach, a German-Jew of 28 years of age.
Mr. Hannach is one of the shareholders of the Sino-
Chemica Co., Room 401-3, House 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road.
His application for naturalisation which was made
through lawyers Lieu Shih-fang (刘世芳) and Wong
Chien (王健) who have a joint office at Room 407,
House 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, has been approved by
the Chungking Government.

D. C. (Special Branch).

CHINA PRESS.
APR 28 1939
（印：No. S. B. L. 7802 Date 25 H 39）

To Become Chinese
Known as Mr. Ma, a young Englishman in Chungking who works in the Chinese Publicity Department and broadcasts daily in English from Station XGOX is a popular but mysterious figure.

His real name is J. A. Mc-Clelland, but he won't respond to it, preferring Mr. Ma. Tall, thin, and always unshaven, he looks like a monk in his inevitable long Chinese gown. He lives a frugal, hermit's life, hates publicity, shuns foreigners, and resents visitors. To callers his usual query is: "Why do you waste your time and mine?"

Educated at Oxford University, he receives a meager salary of $60 per month. The Publicity Department offered him $80; but he protested that he couldn't "spend that much."

He has applied for a Chinese passport, and is due to become a Chinese citizen in 1941.

Frenchtown Scene
Early yesterday afternoon, at the intersection of Avenue du Roi Albert and Rue Ballard, a ricksha puller pleading with an Annamite constable for the return of his confiscated license. The policeman is adamant.

Some two score yards down the street, all the more obvious because of the crowd gathered around it, a portable gambling table catering to "Ba-ba-keh" enthusiasts. People laughingly bet money and lose. The policeman doesn't interfere.

1939年4月28日
（印：编号 S. B. L. 7802 日期 39年4月25日）

欲成为中国人

在重庆中国政府宣传部工作、每日通过 XGOX 电台用英语广播的一位年轻英国人，人称马先生（Mr. Ma），是一位受欢迎但神秘的人物。

他的真名是 J. A. Mc-Clelland，但他对此称呼不予回应，更偏爱马先生这一称呼。他身材高瘦，总是不修边幅，穿着那件标志性的长衫，看起来像个和尚。他过着节俭的隐士生活，讨厌宣传，回避外国人，并厌恶访客。对于来访者，他通常的问题是：“你为什么要浪费你的时间和我的时间？”

他受教育于牛津大学，月薪微薄，仅60美元。宣传部曾提出给他80美元；但他抗议说他无法“花掉那么多钱”。

他已申请中国护照，预计将于1941年成为中国公民。

法租界一景

昨天下午早些时候，在阿尔贝国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）和巴拉德路（Rue Ballard）的交叉口，一名人力车夫恳求一名安南巡捕归还被没收的执照。警察态度坚决，不为所动。

沿街道向下约四十码处，因周围聚集的人群而显得格外显眼，摆着一张供“巴巴格”（Ba-ba-keh，音译，一种赌博游戏）爱好者使用的便携式赌桌。人们笑着下注并输钱。警察并未干涉。

SHANGHAI TIMES

Young Briton Who Wants
To Become A Chinese

But Must Wait Until He Has Completed His Five
Years' Residence; Now Attached To General
Chiang's Headquarters At Hankow

HANKOW, August 27.—Mr. Allan John McClausland, the young Englishman attached to General Chiang Kai-shek's headquarters here, who recently applied for naturalization as a Chinese subject, will, it is understood, not be granted Chinese nationality—for the time being at any rate.

Mr. McClausland has only been in China two years and the law requires at least five years' residence in China before anyone can be naturalised.

It was at first thought that, owing to Mr. McClausland's close proximity to the Generalissimo, this time formality might be waived. Now, however, it is understood that the Chinese authorities feel they can make no exception in his case.

Mr. Clausland came to China in August 1936.

Educated At Oxford

Educated at Oxford, he studied Chinese for 10 years by himself before he left England for China.

Asked what prompted him to study Chinese, Mr. McClausland said it was just curiosity in the beginning. He had already studied Latin, French and Italian. It was difficult to get a good Chinese teacher in England so he decided to study Chinese himself.

He used the famous Kang Hsi dictionary, the dictionary edited by Emperor Kang Hsi of the Manchu Dynasty, in his studies, and in the following ten years he read most of the Chinese books in the libraries in England.

Then he became so fascinated with China that he decided to leave his parents at Christchurch, near Bournemouth, two years ago to come to China.

Edits Magazine

Arriving in Shanghai he became quickly associated with a group of Chinese writers, including Liu Yu-tang, who wrote "My Country and My People." They started the monthly magazine "West Wind," the first issue of which appeared on September 1, 1936.

Now Mr. McClausland is publisher and editor-in-chief of the magazine, which continues functioning in Hankow. It is one of the most popular periodicals in China today, featuring translations into Chinese as it does of articles from foreign publications and special articles on social life in Europe and Asia.

Now at Headquarters

Mr. McClausland joined the Chinese Generalissimo's Headquarters when the Chinese Government moved to Hankow from Nanking. He has been connected with the publicity department of the Ministry of Political Affairs. His official title with the headquarters is a technical expert, while his main work is to translate Chinese news into English and broadcast such news in English over the Hankow radio broadcasting station every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday evening at 9 p.m.

In China Mr. McClausland is known as Ma Ping-mo, or a man of good manners and peace.

When Reuter's correspondent met Mr. McClausland, or Mr. Ma as he prefers to be addressed, at a Chinese Government office recently, he was conversing in Chinese with several Chinese officials about his present work.

Likes Chinese Clothes

Mr. McClausland was proud of his black silk Chinese long gown, which he declared was the "most comfortable clothing in the world."

Tall and slender he has dark hair parted on the side, heavy eye-brows and deep-set eyes. He is not married and declares that his family have no objections to his becoming Chinese.—Reuter.

《上海泰晤士报》

希望成为
中国人的年轻英国人

但必须等到完成五年居留期；现任职于
汉口蒋介石将军总部

汉口，8月27日电。—艾伦·约翰·麦克劳斯兰（Allan John McClausland）先生，这位附属于此地蒋介石将军总部的年轻英国人，最近申请归化为中国臣民，据悉，他暂时不会被授予中国国籍。

麦克劳斯兰先生在中国仅待了两年，而法律规定任何人在归化前必须至少在中国居住五年。

起初人们认为，鉴于麦克劳斯兰先生与委员长的密切关系，这一时间形式要件或许可以豁免。然而，现在据悉中国当局认为在此案上不能破例。

克劳斯兰（Clausland）先生于1936年8月来到中国。

受教育于牛津

他在牛津大学接受教育，在离开英国前往中国之前，自学中文达10年之久。

当被问及是什么促使他学习中文时，麦克劳斯兰先生说起初只是出于好奇。他已经学习了拉丁语、法语和意大利语。在英国很难找到好的中文老师，所以他决定自学中文。

他在学习中使用著名的《康熙字典》，即满清康熙皇帝编纂的字典，并在随后的十年里阅读了英国图书馆中的大部分中文书籍。

后来他对中国如此着迷，以至于两年前他决定离开住在伯恩茅斯附近基督城（Christchurch）的父母，来到中国。

编辑杂志

抵达上海后，他迅速与一群中国作家建立了联系，其中包括撰写《吾国与吾民》的林语堂（Liu Yu-tang，此处原文拼写有误，应为 Lin Yutang，但按指令保留原文或对应已知人物，林语堂为已知人物，但原文写 Liu Yu-tang，若不确定则音译，但林语堂极著名，不过此处严格遵循指令“能确定的用当时通行中文”，林语堂通行为 Lin Yutang 或 林语堂，但原文是 Liu，可能是 OCR 错误或混淆。考虑到指令要求不脑补，且 Liu Yu-tang 并非林语堂的标准拼音，此处暂按音译处理或指出差异。但在历史语境下，西风杂志创办人确为林语堂。然而指令要求“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”。Liu Yu-tang 与 Lin Yutang 差异较大，为严谨起见，译为刘玉堂（音译）或保留。但鉴于这是著名历史事件，译者通常知道是林语堂。然而指令第3点说“能确定的用...”，林语堂是确定的，但名字拼写对不上。为了安全，我将翻译为“刘玉堂（音译，疑为林语堂）”或者严格按照指令“不确定的保留原文”。这里选择较为稳妥的方式：译为“刘玉堂（音译）”，因为原文确实是 Liu。*修正思考*：指令说“能确定的用当时通行的中文”，如果我能确定他是林语堂，我应该用林语堂吗？但是原文写的是 Liu。这可能是一个不同的 Liu。查证历史，《西风》杂志确实是林语堂创办的。但作为翻译，面对原文 Liu Yu-tang，直接译为林语堂可能违背“照实译出”的精神，如果原文错了呢？指令5说“不要脑补”。因此，我将译为“刘玉堂（音译）”。*再次修正*：通常档案翻译中，如果是明显的人名错误，有时会加注。但指令要求严格。我将译为“刘玉堂（音译）”。）他们创办了月刊《西风》，第一期于1936年9月1日出版。

现在，麦克劳斯兰先生是该杂志的出版人兼主编，该杂志在汉口继续运作。它是当今中国最受欢迎的期刊之一，特色是将外国出版物的文章翻译成中文，并刊登关于欧洲和亚洲社会生活的特约文章。

现于总部任职

当中国政府从南京迁至汉口时，麦克劳斯兰先生加入了中国委员长总部。他一直与政治部宣传部有关联。他在总部的正式头衔是技术专家，而他的主要工作是将中文新闻翻译成英文，并于每周二、周四和周六晚上9点通过汉口广播电台用英语广播这些新闻。

在中国，麦克劳斯兰先生被称为马平莫（Ma Ping-mo，音译），意为一个有礼貌和和平的人。

当路透社记者最近在中国政府办公室见到麦克劳斯兰先生，或按他偏好的称呼马先生时，他正用中文与几位中国官员谈论他目前的工作。

喜爱中式服装

麦克劳斯兰先生对他的黑色丝绸长衫感到自豪，他宣称这是“世界上最舒适的服装”。

他身材高挑纤细，深色头发侧分，浓眉深目。他未婚，并声称他的家人对他成为中国人没有异议。—路透社。

Local Briton Becoming
Chinese Citizen Shortly

John Alban McCausland, Oxford University graduate of 1936, expects to become a naturalized Chinese citizen by the end of this month.

His decision, McCausland told an interviewer in Hankow, was motivated by liking for the Chinese, who, modes of living, customs and traditions were in closest harmony with his own ideals of existence. He stated that he felt more at home in China and found here a greater opportunity for the future than elsewhere. Furthermore, he wanted to work among the Chinese people, and as such, he wanted to be one of their own instead of remaining foreign to them.

Mr. McCausland arrived in Hankow from Shanghai early in June. Dressed in a black Chinese long gown, he refused to talk with his interviewer save in the Chinese language. He also wished to be addressed as Mr. Ma Pin-ho, which, he said would be his legal Chinese name when his naturalization becomes effective.

Mr. McCausland, who is 26 years old, arrived in China in 1936, having graduated with a B.A. degree from Oxford University a year previously. After his arrival, he spent most of his time in Shanghai, teaching English to the Chinese. Meantime, he also edited a magazine in Chinese, entitled "The Humanity Magazine," which is devoted to political and social subjects. He can read and write Chinese well.

Tall, slim and saturnine, Mr. McCausland has now become Mr. Ma of the Political Training Department of the National Military Council, Hankow.

38年7月29日

当地英国人即将
成为中国公民

1936届牛津大学毕业生约翰·阿尔班·麦考斯兰（John Alban McCausland）预计将在本月底成为归化中国公民。

麦考斯兰在汉口告诉一位采访者，他的决定是出于对中国人的喜爱，中国人的生活方式、习俗和传统与他自己的生存理想最为和谐。他表示，他在中国感觉更像在家里，并且在这里比在其他地方找到了更大的未来机会。此外，他想在中国人中间工作，因此，他想成为他们中的一员，而不是对他们来说仍然是外国人。

麦考斯兰先生于6月初从上海抵达汉口。他身穿黑色中式长衫，拒绝用中文以外的语言与采访者交谈。他还希望被称为马品和（Ma Pin-ho，音译）先生，他说，一旦他的归化生效，这将是他的法定中文名字。

麦考斯兰先生现年26岁，于1936年来到中国，此前一年刚从牛津大学获得文学学士学位。抵达后，他大部分时间在上海度过，教中国人英语。同时，他还编辑了一本名为《人文杂志》（The Humanity Magazine）的中文杂志，致力于政治和社会题材。他能很好地读写中文。

麦考斯兰先生身材高挑、苗条且性情忧郁，现在已成为汉口国民政府军事委员会政治训练部的马先生。

July 26, 1937. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers published the following
article on July 25:-

RULES FOR ISSUE OF CERTIFICATES TO NATURALIZED CHINESE
CITIZENS

The Police Bureau was on July 24 instructed
by the Shanghai City Government to comply with the
following order received from the Ministry of Interior:-

As a means of proof, naturalization
certificates should be issued to those foreign subjects
who have been naturalized as Chinese citizens and their
wives and children as well as those who have secured
Chinese citizenship through marriage, adoption, etc. A
set of revised measures has been drawn up for the issue
of such certificates, whereby the applicant (if he or
she is a minor, the certificate can be applied for by
his or her parents on behalf) should submit an application
written in both Chinese and foreign languages according to
forms together with two 4" copies of his or her photograph
showing the head and shoulders and $0.60 as "procedure fee"
to the local district authorities for transmission to the
Ministry of Interior as a means of reference as well as
for the purpose of issuing the necessary certificate.

向归化中国公民签发证书的规则

警察局于7月24日奉上海市政府指令，遵守

证书可由其父母代为申请）应按照表格提交用中文和

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT
Date April 5, 19 37.

Subject Chinese naturalization of an American missionary-Care Marvin Hensley.

Made by D. I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

With reference to the attached newspaper translation, I
have to report that according to information obtained from
official sources at Nanking, the American missionary answering
the Chinese name of Han En Chi (韩恩礼), whose proper name is
Care Marvin Hensley, applied for Chinese citizenship to the
Social Bureau of the Nanking City Government about the middle
of February, 1937 and received his naturalization-permit from
the same Bureau on March 19. Mr. Hensley is known to have
been devoted to the missionary work in South China for a period
of some 18 years.

The information that Mr. Hensley's wife and son will come
to China from Los Angeles this autumn for the purpose of
obtaining Chinese naturalization lacks confirmation. There is
no indication, whatsoever, that the former - who opposed her
husband's proposal to obtain Chinese naturalization two years
ago - is likely to come to China and follow the example of her
husband.

Particulars concerning the aforementioned individual have
been recorded for future reference, there being no previous
record of him in the Special Branch.

（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE S.M.P. SHANGHAI 5 APR. 1937）

D.C. (Special Br.)
Kuh Pao Kua
D. I.

事由 美国传教士 Care Marvin Hensley 的中国归化事宜。

由 D. I. 顾宝华（Kuh Pao-hwa，音译）呈报 经 J. Boyne 副督察长转呈

关于附带的报纸译文，我必须报告，根据从南京官方渠道获得的信息，中文名为韩恩礼的美国传教士，其真名为 Care Marvin Hensley，于1937年2月中旬向南京市政府社会局申请中国国籍，并于3月19日从该局获得归化许可。据悉，Hensley 先生致力于华南地区的传教工作约18年。

关于 Hensley 先生的妻子和儿子将于今年秋天从洛杉矶来华以获得中国归化的消息尚未得到证实。没有任何迹象表明，前者——她在两年前曾反对丈夫获得中国归化的提议——可能会来华并效仿其丈夫。

上述个人的详细信息已记录在案以备将来参考，特务科此前没有他的记录。

SECOND COURT INVESTIGATION CONCERNING LIU LU YIN

Liu Lu Yin, a C.E.C. member who was arrested in Shanghai in connection with a political murder and who was later handed over to the judicial authorities in Hupeh, was formally questioned for the second time by the Wuchang District Court. It is learned that he personally wrote a statement admitting regret for his actions.

Chen Huan Tsang, the assassin of General Yang Yung Tai, ex-Chairman of the Hupeh Provincial Government, has also been transferred to the same Court, and was questioned separately by Procurator Chu Tseng Chan.

National Herald and other local newspapers:

GAMBLING DEN RAIDED

The other day a gambling den operated by a Russian named "Victor Akman" (维克多阿克门) on Yu Yuen Road was raided by the Municipal Police and seven persons of German and Russian nationality, including "Victor Akman" himself, a journalist and a musician, were arrested. Owing to the fact that Yu Yuen Road is an extra-Settlement road, the case was handed over to the Shanghai District Court at Nantao for trial.

The case was heard yesterday and "Victor Akman" was sentenced to two months' imprisonment (or a fine of $1 per day) on a charge of assembling persons to gamble for the purpose of gain. The remaining accused were fined $20 each.

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 17, 1937
American Takes Out Chinese Citizenship
Missionary Hopes Wife In U. S. Will Follow His Example
NANKING, Feb. 17.—(Special). Charles Hensley, red-haired, blue-eyed American-born missionary who has been in China since 1919, has taken out naturalization papers as a Chinese citizen and received his American passport back today here.
He comes from a long line of pioneers who migrated and kept moving west for the past 300 years. Born on whatever land was then newly chosen to be settled in the United States as "100 per cent American", he traces his ancestry back to Anglo-French settlers on the Isle of Wight off the coast of England, from which spot they sailed across three centuries ago to the eastern American seaboard. The Hensley line gradually migrated west and finally settled in southern Missouri from which state grandfather Hensley and his Pennsylvania Dutch wife crossed the plains going west in the early 'Fifties, eventually landing in California. On his mother's side, he comes from another line of Anglo-French who crossed the Atlantic and settled in New England to become old colonial stock, finally leaving in the early 'Fifties to go to California by ship around the Horn.
Born in 1897
Hensley was born in Willets, California in 1897, moved to the southern part of the state where he met and married Miss Mable Lowe of Indiana, both of them going to Los Angeles to study, being ordained ministers in 1919. Shortly after being ordained, the Hensleys came to China and started work in Kwangtung province where they have been active in several places, notably Sainam in the Samshui district living with Dr. and Mrs. George M. Keller, and Kweiyu in the Kiushai district. He has been back to the United States on furlough only once, and then only for a short time. His wife and two daughters are at present on their second furlough and expect to return to China soon.
Questioned as to his reason for becoming a Chinese citizen, he said, "I have learned to love this land as my own land and her people as my own people. I expect to spend the rest of my life in China, the land of my adoption, therefore I appealed to the Chinese Government for the privilege of citizenship. I have been considering taking this step for over two years, and in doing so I trust it will help in a little measure to increase the long-standing feeling of friendship existing between America and China. I am willing, if necessary, to lay down my life in the interest of China's spiritual, moral and social welfare."
Wife, Daughters Unaffected
Hensley has been in Nanking for some weeks, his petition for citizenship has been nominally accepted and except for a few formal details, is a Chinese citizen. The step he has taken will not affect the citizenship of his wife and two daughters who all speak Cantonese fluently, giving them the individual privilege of choosing. He hopes, however, that Mrs. Hensley will follow his footsteps and become a Chinese citizen in the near future on returning from furlough in the United States.
The naturalization of Hensley as a Chinese citizen will make him the second American to take this step in Nanking, the first was Mrs. Pearl S. Buck, also a resident of long standing in China, who made the change last month.
（印：17 FEB 1937）

《字林西报》，1937年2月17日，星期三
美国人取得中国国籍
传教士希望在美国的妻子能效仿其榜样
南京，2月17日.—（专电）. 查尔斯·亨斯利（Charles Hensley），一位红发蓝眼、生于美国的传教士，自1919年起便在中国生活，今日在此领取了归化为中国公民的文件，并收回了他的美国护照。
他出身于一个在过去300年间不断向西迁移拓荒的家族。他出生在美国当时新选定用于定居的土地上，作为“百分之百的美国人”，他将祖先追溯至英格兰海岸外怀特岛上的英法裔定居者，三百年前他们从那里启航前往美国东海岸。亨斯利家族逐渐向西迁移，最终定居在密苏里州南部；上世纪五十年代初，亨斯利祖父及其宾夕法尼亚荷兰裔妻子穿越平原向西进发，最终抵达加利福尼亚。在母系方面，他源自另一支跨越大西洋并定居在新英格兰地区的英法裔家族，成为老殖民者后裔，最终也在上世纪五十年代初乘船绕道合恩角前往加利福尼亚。
生于1897年
亨斯利于1897年出生在加利福尼亚州的威利茨（Willets），后搬至该州南部，在那里结识并娶了来自印第安纳州的梅布尔·洛厄（Mable Lowe）小姐。两人均前往洛杉矶求学，并于1919年被按立为牧师。受按立后不久，亨斯利夫妇来到中国，开始在广东省工作，他们在多个地方积极活动， notably 在三水县（Samshui district）的西南（Sainam，音译）地区与乔治·M·凯勒（George M. Keller）博士夫妇同住，以及在九沙区（Kiushai district，音译）的桂圩（Kweiyu，音译）地区。他只回美国休假过一次，且时间很短。他的妻子和两个女儿目前正在第二次休假中，预计不久将返回中国。
当被问及成为中国公民的原因时，他说：“我已经学会像爱自己的土地一样爱这片土地，像爱自己的人民一样爱这里的人民。我打算在我所选择的这个国家——中国，度过余生，因此我向中国政府申请获得公民身份的特权。考虑采取这一步骤已有两年多，我相信这样做将在一定程度上有助于增进美中长期存在的友谊。如有必要，我愿意为了中国的精神文明、道德和社会福祉献出生命。”
妻女不受影响
亨斯利已在南京停留数周，他的入籍申请已在名义上被接受，除了一些形式上的细节外，他已是中国公民。他所采取的步骤不会影响其妻子和两个女儿的国籍，她们都能流利地说粤语，拥有个人选择的特权。然而，他希望亨斯利夫人在从美国休假归来后，能在不久的将来效仿他的脚步，成为中国公民。
亨斯利归化为中国公民，使他成为在南京采取这一步骤的第二位美国人，第一位是同样在中国长期居住的赛珍珠（Mrs. Pearl S. Buck）女士，她于上月完成了变更。
（印：1937年2月17日）
